name: Question 12
problem:
Given the functions $f(x),g(x)$ and $h(x)$ below, which of them has a jump discontinuity at $x=7?$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={\begin{aligned}2x-1, & x\le 7 \\ {x}^{2}-30, & x>7,\end{aligned} \\ g(x) & ={\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}, & x<7 \\ 5x+14, & x\ge 7,\end{aligned} \\ h(x) & ={\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{x-7}, & x<7 \\ \frac{1}{7}, & x\ge 7,\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
For $f(x),$ let's go through our continuity checklist:

- $f(7)=2(7)-1=13$ exists $\,\,✓$

- Let's now check the left and right limits. We see that

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{7}^{-}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,{7}^{-}}(2x-1)=2(7)-1=13
$$

while

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{7}^{+}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,{7}^{+}}({x}^{2}-30)={7}^{2}-30=19.
$$

So both the left and right limits exist and are finite, but they are not equal.$\,\,\times $

Therefore, $f(x)$ has a jump discontinuity at $x=7.$

Now, for $g(x),$ let's go through our continuity checklist:

- $g(7)=5(7)+14=49$ exists $\,\,✓$

- Let's now check the left and right limits. We see that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,{7}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \,{7}^{-}}{x}^{2}=49, \\ {lim}_{x\to \,{7}^{+}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \,{7}^{+}}(5x+14)=5(7)+14=49.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the overall limit exists and ${lim}_{x\to 7}f(x)=49.\,\,✓$ $\,\,\,$

- Finally, we check that the value of the limit equals the value of the function: 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,7}g(x)=49=g(7).\,\,✓
$$

Therefore, $g(x)$ is continuous at $x=7.$

For $h(x),$ let's go through our continuity checklist:

- $h(7)=\frac{1}{7}$ exists $\,\,✓$

- Let's now check the left and right limits. We see that

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{7}^{-}}h(x)={lim}_{x\to \,{7}^{-}}\frac{1}{x-7}=-\infty 
$$

while

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{7}^{+}}h(x)={lim}_{x\to \,{7}^{+}}\frac{1}{7}=\frac{1}{7}.
$$

Since the left limit is infinite, $h(x)$ does not have a jump discontinuity at $x=7.$

Question 12

Given the functions f(x),g(x) and h(x) below, which of them has a jump discontinuity at x=7?

f(x)={2x−1,x≤7x2−30,x>7,g(x)={x2,x<75x+14,x≥7,h(x)={1x−7,x<717,x≥7,

a
g(x) and h(x) only
b
g(x) only
c
h(x) only
d
f(x) and g(x) only
e
f(x) only
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For f(x), let's go through our continuity checklist:

  • f(7)=2(7)−1=13 exists ✓

  • Let's now check the left and right limits. We see that limx→7−f(x)=limx→7−(2x−1)=2(7)−1=13 while limx→7+f(x)=limx→7+(x2−30)=72−30=19. So both the left and right limits exist and are finite, but they are not equal.×

Therefore, f(x) has a jump discontinuity at x=7.

Now, for g(x), let's go through our continuity checklist:

  • g(7)=5(7)+14=49 exists ✓

  • Let's now check the left and right limits. We see that limx→7−g(x)=limx→7−x2=49,limx→7+g(x)=limx→7+(5x+14)=5(7)+14=49. Therefore, the overall limit exists and limx→7f(x)=49.✓

  • Finally, we check that the value of the limit equals the value of the function: limx→7g(x)=49=g(7).✓

Therefore, g(x) is continuous at x=7.

For h(x), let's go through our continuity checklist:

  • h(7)=17 exists ✓

  • Let's now check the left and right limits. We see that limx→7−h(x)=limx→7−1x−7=−∞ while limx→7+h(x)=limx→7+17=17.

Since the left limit is infinite, h(x) does not have a jump discontinuity at x=7.
